ca_june_lake_bouldering.blurb: Boulder fields scattered around June Lake in the Eastern Sierra, a short distance off the main valley highway and roughly 7,600 feet up. This is almost purely bouldering. Most problems sit in the easy to moderate range, with a solid spread of mid-grade lines and a thinner tail of hard V5 to V9 testpieces. The stone is mostly volcanic tuff, with some granite nearer the village. Hartley Springs, the biggest cluster, spreads its blocks through Jeffrey pine forest, mostly with flat pumice landings, and at about 8,200 feet it climbs from spring through late fall. North Shore Drive and Deadman Summit add roadside venues. Compared with the better-known, lower and hotter Eastern Sierra boulder fields, expect quiet and plenty of space.

or_cline_falls_bouldering.blurb: A compact basalt venue on the Deschutes River in Central Oregon, a few miles west of Redmond. The place is dominated by bouldering, with a few short trad and sport lines on top. The bulk of the problems fall between V0 and V4, with a thinner sprinkling of harder lines up to V10. Roped climbs mostly sit around 5.9 to 5.10. A west-facing cliff just below the falls holds the routes, while the boulders spread downstream along the river, mainly in the East section with a smaller West section. In summer the cliff stays shaded until mid-afternoon. Higher river flows in fall and winter can change how you reach the rocks.

ca_lassen_area.blurb: Crags and boulders in and around Lassen Volcanic National Park, where the Sierra and Cascades meet in Northeast California. The mix is wide: bouldering, trad, alpine, sport and top-rope all appear, with roped climbs clustered around 5.10 and 5.11 and a good number of easier ones. Rock is volcanic. Inside the park, crags such as Eagle Peak, The Plug and Raker Peak are spread out, and most need a long walk. Warner Valley is a woodland setting with west-facing crags, the Loading Zone leaning trad and the Fallout Zone mostly bolted, where shade is easy to find and spring through fall is the usual window. The stone there is mostly crumbly volcanic with small fine-grained basalt pockets.

mt_hyalite_canyon.blurb: A canyon just south of Bozeman that is best known for winter ice: waterfalls that run through summer freeze into a huge range of routes, from long-established lines to formations that last a single season. Ice is the largest share here, mostly WI3 to WI5, with a deep layer of mixed climbing from M3 up to M11. Away from the cold months there is rock too, plus bouldering, trad and sport, mostly 5.10 to 5.12. The Genesis area is the hub for ice, and Practice Rock at the north end offers nearly every style within a short drive of town. The canyons around Bozeman are generally climbable from spring through fall, and the closest roadside crags can be busy and noisy.

ar_sam_s_throne.blurb: A hard sandstone climbing area in the Boston Mountains of north-central Arkansas, set in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest. Traditional climbing is the main event, with sport routes and a smaller group of boulders alongside. Difficulty centers on 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent run of 5.8 and 5.9 below and a few 5.12s and 5.13s above. Because most routes need your own protection, it suits climbers with solid technical skills rather than beginners. The cliffs are split into several faces and zones, including East Main Bluff, The Throne, The Outback and West Main Bluff, so a visit can fill several days across different aspects.

nv_reno_area.blurb: A year-round climbing base in western Nevada, sitting in the Sierra Nevada rain shadow with a relatively mild climate. Bouldering is the biggest piece, mostly easy to moderate problems, followed by sport climbing, mainly 5.9 to 5.12, and a smaller amount of trad and top-rope. Owl Rock is the best-known crag, a high desert sport wall where you can chase shade or sun through the day. River Rock offers trad lines, and Thomas Creek and Mogul Cliffs add a bit more. Reno itself has limited climbing, but the Donner Summit and the Tahoe crags lie within about an hour or two, and Highway 395 runs south toward the High Sierra.
